title: Runtime semantic versioning & gated rollout playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Define a single, operationally actionable semantic versioning policy for the serving runtime that unambiguously categorizes changes (breaking, additive, patch fixes), pairs each category with LTS channel guarantees, and prescribes automated rollout gates and upgrade tooling to make upgrades predictable for customers. Scope covers: public runtime API (HTTP/GRPC), on-disk model/quantization artifacts, KV cache binary formats, runtime feature flags and config schemas, client SDK compatibility promises, and console-facing rollout controls.

Why this ticket exists: multiple teams ship runtime changes with divergent expectations about compatibility and rollback. We need a concise playbook that engineers can apply at PR time and release time so that customers experience minimal surprises. This doc is the canonical policy + actionable checklist + links to tooling automation (release-cli, upgrade-checker, canary orchestration).
acceptance_criteria: A one-page semantic versioning summary for runtime owners that maps change types to version increments and LTS commitments.
A gating checklist that is enforced by release CI: compatibility tests, migration smoke, canary health checks, and customer-impact assessment.
Automated release-cli flags that annotate PRs with change class (breaking|additive|patch) and require reviewer acknowledgement for breaking changes.
Upgrade tooling (upgrade-checker) that can run in customers' CI to detect incompatible client/behavioral changes before rolling out.
Playbook includes rollback triggers and a documented 72-hour observability window for any runtime MAJOR or MINOR rollout with non-zero canary percentage.
rollout_plan: Channels: runtime-2.x-lts (18 month supported), runtime-stable (6 month supported), runtime-edge (nightly). Versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. MAJOR increments may include breaking API or on-disk format changes and require explicit opt-in migration; MINOR increments may include additive features and non-breaking behavioral changes; PATCH increments limited to bug fixes and security patches. Gate strategy: PR classification + automated compatibility matrix run in CI -> staged canary (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback on SLO violations (latency > baseline+30% or error-rate > baseline+1%). Canary windows: 24h at 1%, 12h at 10%, 6h at 50% unless critical customer impact indicated. Rollout automation will use release-cli with --change-class, --canary-sequence, and --migration-script fields.
decision_log: We treat wire-protocol and on-disk artifact changes as breaking by default; compatibility shims must be shipped as separate MINOR releases or toggled features.
Backward-incompatible telemetry schema changes must be sharded behind an opt-in header and billed as MAJOR changes.
Patch releases are allowed to alter request validation but not response contracts for existing routes; any response contract change moves to MINOR.
We deprioritized keeping binary plugin API stable across majors; instead we will provide compatibility helpers and migration scripts to reduce long-term maintenance cost.
test_plan: Compatibility suite that runs client SDK tests against new runtime image: smoke, request/response shape, tokenization edge cases.
Fuzz tests for KV cache eviction and cache-key stability between versions.
Performance regression benchmarks: 95th latency and p95 token throughput compared against baseline on representative hardware profiles.
Canary health probes including synthetic prompts, model LLM-quality regression sentinel prompts, and quota/permission checks for private deployments.
Upgrade-path validation: run migration scripts in a sandbox with model artifacts and quantization profiles to ensure successful startup.
migration_guidance: Always pin client SDK to the highest MINOR compatible with your runtime MAJOR; include compatibility headers to opt into new MINOR features.
When changing MAJOR: provide migration script in the release PR, add sample terraform snippets for Dedicated/Private customers, and include rollback instructions for config and key vault changes.
Provide an 'upgrade-checker' docker image that customers can run against their artifacts to preview incompatibilities before scheduling the upgrade window.
Document common failure modes (KV cache mismatch, quantization ABI changes, model artifact version mismatches) and how to remediate them.
